## Findings

I could not verify **which specific Medicaid managed‑care organization (MCO)** issued this denial. The notice identifies the plan only as "Medicaid (Medicaid), state of New Mexico" — it does not name the MCO administering the benefit. As of July 1, 2024, New Mexico's Medicaid managed‑care program ("Turquoise Care") is administered through **four separate MCOs**, each of which maintains its **own** medical‑necessity policy for total hip arthroplasty (CPT 27130):

- Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Mexico (BCBSNM)
- Presbyterian Health Plan (PHP)
- Molina Healthcare of New Mexico
- UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of New Mexico

I was able to locate a real, NM‑specific, CPT‑27130‑applicable policy for only one of these four (UnitedHealthcare) and a related but not CPT‑27130‑specific joint‑replacement policy for Presbyterian. I found no publicly posted CPT‑27130 medical‑necessity criteria document for BCBSNM or Molina's New Mexico Medicaid plans. Because the denial letter does not state which of the four MCOs sent it, I cannot confirm that either document I found is the one actually applied to this member, and I am not willing to name a document as "the" governing policy without that confirmation.

For transparency, the one concretely on‑point document I found is:

- **UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Medical Policy, "Surgery of the Hip (for New Mexico Only)"**, Policy Number CS056NM.F, Effective Date May 1, 2026, URL: https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/medicaid-comm-plan/nm/surgery-hip-nm-cs.pdf. It states CPT 27130 falls under "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip" and that "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: ... Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip" — a licensed, proprietary criteria set not reproduced in the public document. This document is only usable as the operative policy if the member is in fact enrolled with UnitedHealthcare Community Plan NM — which the letter does not confirm.

## Findings

I could not verify **which specific Medicaid managed‑care organization (MCO)** issued this denial. The notice identifies the plan only as "Medicaid (Medicaid), state of New Mexico" — it does not name the MCO administering the benefit. As of July 1, 2024, New Mexico's Medicaid managed‑care program ("Turquoise Care") is administered through **four separate MCOs**, each of which maintains its **own** medical‑necessity policy for total hip arthroplasty (CPT 27130):

- Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Mexico (BCBSNM)
- Presbyterian Health Plan (PHP)
- Molina Healthcare of New Mexico
- UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of New Mexico

I was able to locate a real, NM‑specific, CPT‑27130‑applicable policy for only one of these four (UnitedHealthcare) and a related but not CPT‑27130‑specific joint‑replacement policy for Presbyterian. I found no publicly posted CPT‑27130 medical‑necessity criteria document for BCBSNM or Molina's New Mexico Medicaid plans. Because the denial letter does not state which of the four MCOs sent it, I cannot confirm that either document I found is the one actually applied to this member, and I am not willing to name a document as "the" governing policy without that confirmation.

For transparency, the one concretely on‑point document I found is:

- **UnitedHealthcare Community Plan Medical Policy, "Surgery of the Hip (for New Mexico Only)"**, Policy Number CS056NM.F, Effective Date May 1, 2026, URL: https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/medicaid-comm-plan/nm/surgery-hip-nm-cs.pdf. It states CPT 27130 falls under "Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip" and that "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: ... Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Hip" — a licensed, proprietary criteria set not reproduced in the public document. This document is only usable as the operative policy if the member is in fact enrolled with UnitedHealthcare Community Plan NM — which the letter does not confirm.
